Installation and Requirements

cuDART is written in C++, and runs on the GPU. As such, to function it requires

  • A CUDA-capable GPU (from Ampere onwards)

  • The nvcc compiler

  • Python (optional, but highly recommended for front-end), with the following modules

    • common modules such as numpy, matplotlib

    • if using data from PLUTO, the pyPLUTO module (available here)

    • if using data in the HDF5 format, the h5py module

Setup

First, clone a local copy of the cuDART codebase

$ git clone git@github.com:hwhitehead/cuDART.git

cuDART is packaged with a template makefile, the user should configure before building

$ export CUDART_DIR=/path/to/cuDART
$ cd $CUDART_DIR
$ python3 configure.py --arch=GPU_ARCH --gpu=GPU_MODEL
$ make clean
$ make

where here the --arch and --gpu flags allow the user to target their own GPU architecture or model. This allows cuDART to build machine-specific code and avoid just-in-time compilation on deployment. If no arguments are passed to configure.py, cuDART will pre-compile GPU-agnostic code valid for any NVIDIA GPU at least as modern as Ampere.

Regression

cuDART comes packaged with regression testing routines to construct mock data and peform a range of rendering operations. These routines can be found at scripts/regression.py. These tests can be invoked from the command line as

$ cd $CUDART_DIR
$ python3 scripts/regression.py <flags>

where the choices for flags are

  • -b invokes the build_unlabelled_regresssion_suite function, generating a series of mock simulation snapshots in time

  • -bl invokes the build_labelled_regression_suite function, generation a series of mock simulation snapshots in time, splitting the simulation into sub-domains for use in labelled model

  • --data_dir=<data_dir> accepts a path to specify the directory in which to generate mock snapshots, and to read from for rendering

  • --save_dir=<save_dir> accepts a path to specificy the directory in which to save raw .npy renders, and .png figures

  • -r invokes the run_nolookback_test routine, which renders a series of images from a single snapshot, varying the camera position

  • -rl involes the run_lookback_test routine, which renders a series of images from multiple snapshots, varying the camera time

  • -v results in additional verbose prints to the terminal

For example, if the user wishes to generate an unlabelled mock data set at $DATA_DIR, render it using the lookback method and save the resulting .npy raw images and .png figures at $SAVE_DIR, they might run the following

$ cd $CUDART_DIR
$ python3 scripts/regression.py -v -bl -rl --data_dir=$DATA_DIR --save_dir=$SAVE_DIR

As both the labelled and unlabelled build routines share the data_dir write space, the two flags cannot be used together. Similarly, the lookback and no-lookback render routines share the save_dir write space, so are also exclusive.
